samples.summary: Persona `id` is interpolated straight into filesystem paths (rubric read, output dir) with no shape validation, and the read happens before `validatePersona` runs
samples.evidence: `loadPersonas` does `readFileSync(path.join(dir, `${p.id}.md`), "utf8")` (hunt-ui.mjs:111) at load time, i.e. BEFORE any validation; `validatePersona` (hunt-ui.mjs:128) only requires `typeof p.id === "string" && p.id !== ""` — it never rejects `/`, `..` or absolute paths. The same id is later joined into an output path that is written to: `const personaDir = path.join(outDir, persona.id)` (hunt-ui.mjs:1357) followed by `writeArtifact(path.join(personaDir, "explore-raw.json"), …)` (hunt-ui.mjs:1412). Attack: a personas.json entry (this diff adds one — charters-ui/personas.json:50) with `"id": "../../../../home/runner/notes"` makes the loader read an arbitrary `*.md` file outside `charters-ui` and embed its contents in the explorer/verifier system prompt as `persona.rubric` (used at hunt-ui.mjs:513-525 / 729-740), i.e. it is shipped to a third-party model API; the same id also writes `explore-raw.json` outside the intended `--out` tree. Mitigations that keep this minor rather than major: the `.md` suffix is appended so reads are confined to markdown files, and personas.json plus `--charters-dir` are repo/operator-controlled, so exploitation needs write access to the branch being run. Note the identical pattern exists for the CLI hunter (`hunt.mjs:104`), so this is pre-existing and not introduced here — but this change is what adds a new manifest entry to that path. A cheap fix is an `/^[a-z0-9-]+$/` id check in `validatePersona`, applied before `loadPersonas` reads anything (or a `path.resolve` containment check on both the rubric path and `personaDir`).

samples.summary: Drift-guard regex is now built by unescaped string interpolation of the surface list
samples.evidence: `new RegExp(`"((?:${UI_SURFACES.join("|")})\\.[A-Za-z]+)":`, "g")` splices `UI_SURFACES` into a pattern with no escaping. Today the values are the trusted identifiers `sheet|doc|slides`, so nothing is exploitable; the weakness is structural — a future surface name containing a regex metacharacter (`.`, `+`, `(`) would either throw or silently change what this guard matches, and this guard is what keeps the advertised reader catalogue pinned to the bridge's closed reader set (the safety property the bridge comments rely on). Escaping the interpolated tokens, or matching `"([A-Za-z]+\.[A-Za-z]+)":` and filtering by `UI_SURFACES.includes(namespace)`, removes the dynamic-pattern construction entirely.
